Both inverse signs from the same selected transition must match to veto a fresh neighbor. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph even when its score is worse, and a separate archive retains the best score. The current deletion choices remove one leaf atom or contract one degree-two atom, so removal of a longer pendant substituent requires several separately evaluated transitions. approach.novelty: Extend the existing deletion menu with a whole pendant-branch choice. When the deletion operator is drawn, it may remove an entire acyclic substituent attached through one single bond to a ring atom, while retaining every ring atom and the connections among retained atoms. Single-leaf choices remain in the same menu, and the operator keeps its existing allocation weight. This adds direct compact neighbors that no existing one-step removal can reach. The earlier sulfur sibling filtered local valence; this experiment changes the size of a permitted deletion and does not inherit or add that filter.

hypothesis: Extend the Parent's existing uniformly sampled leaf-deletion menu with whole multi-atom acyclic branches attached by one non-ring single bond directly to a ring atom, so the same deletion-operator allocation can emit a compact neighbor in one edit while retaining the complete ring framework.

finding_summary.headline: Whole-branch deletion produced compact neighbors, but every score replica regressed.
finding_summary.insights:
A lack of eligible branches was not the bottleneck: the Parent already had branch opportunities in 399 of 435 states, and the extension successfully turned such opportunities into new evaluated neighbors. The added prunings usually lost source score, rarely won their batch and were followed by regrowth whenever selected. Those observations help explain why immediate reductions of several atoms did not produce a lasting shift toward smaller sampled molecules under the unchanged accepted-score walk.

The experiment separates direct access to compact analogues from retaining useful score. Its complete method loses score in every seed, although that loss cannot be assigned solely to the pruned candidates because the changed menu also changes later sampling and trajectories. The molecular assessment remains dominated by sulfur-rich polycycles, reactive heteroatom bonds and unresolved ring geometry and stereochemistry. Ring-preserving removal alone does not resolve those chemical limitations.
finding_summary.results:
The expanded menu was available in 391 of 435 actual batch-start states. It selected 83 whole-branch edits, all graph-valid; after seven duplicate exclusions and seven tabu vetoes, 69 prunings reached evaluation. Each removed 2-14 heavy atoms in one step, averaging 3.75 atoms and 2.10 rotatable bonds, while retaining every ring atom and bond. The recorded menus, uniform selection, graph edits and identity joins passed the audit, including exact original behavior in all 55 deletion draws where no added branch was available.

Eight of the 69 evaluated prunings beat their source, and four became the next current state. All four later grew again. Typical emitted size remained essentially unchanged at 33.21 heavy atoms, compared with 33.20 for Parent. All three seeds completed their five 300-evaluation tasks; sampling cost was also similar at 12.14 versus 12.15 attempts per ten-member batch.

Mean macro final Top-1 fell from 0.520918 to 0.456635, a paired mean change of -0.064283. The three seed changes were -0.020009, -0.101316 and -0.071524. Every task mean declined, with the largest losses in DRD2 and sitagliptin. The intended neighborhood expansion and immediate size reduction occurred, while the score-retention hypothesis failed on the supplied panel.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

finding_summary.insights:

finding_summary.insights:
A lack of eligible branches was not the bottleneck: the Parent already had branch opportunities in 399 of 435 states, and the extension successfully turned such opportunities into new evaluated neighbors. The added prunings usually lost source score, rarely won their batch and were followed by regrowth whenever selected. Those observations help explain why immediate reductions of several atoms did not produce a lasting shift toward smaller sampled molecules under the unchanged accepted-score walk.

The experiment separates direct access to compact analogues from retaining useful score. Its complete method loses score in every seed, although that loss cannot be assigned solely to the pruned candidates because the changed menu also changes later sampling and trajectories. The molecular assessment remains dominated by sulfur-rich polycycles, reactive heteroatom bonds and unresolved ring geometry and stereochemistry. Ring-preserving removal alone does not resolve those chemical limitations.

finding_summary.insights:

The added prunings usually lost source score, rarely won their batch and were followed by regrowth whenever selected. Those observations help explain why immediate reductions of several atoms did not produce a lasting shift toward smaller sampled molecules under the unchanged accepted-score walk.

The experiment separates direct access to compact analogues from retaining useful score. Its complete method loses score in every seed, although that loss cannot be assigned solely to the pruned candidates because the changed menu also changes later sampling and trajectories. The molecular assessment remains dominated by sulfur-rich polycycles, reactive heteroatom bonds and unresolved ring geometry and stereochemistry. Ring-preserving removal alone does not resolve those chemical limitations.

molecular_assessment.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete corresponding Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 trajectories. Ring-closure and branch presence are 1.0 throughout. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.7322 to 1.0, while charge and stereocentre token presence remain 0.0. These counters indicate SMILES features, not aromatic atom fractions, measured basicity or feasible stereochemistry. The output remains chemically close in broad character to the Parent: compact fused aromatic carbonyl compounds, large decorated nitrogen heterocycles, halogenated aromatic amine assemblies, bridged oxygen/nitrogen carbonyl systems and sulfur-rich cages. Several seeds change detailed scaffolds, giving moderate diversity across the panel, but each late trajectory mainly varies a related family. The more conventional indole or aza-indole amides coexist with multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur, sulfur-carbon triple bonds, N-Cl/N-F/O-F bonds, peroxides and extensive constrained ring closure. Overall synthetic plausibility remains poor and drug-like quality weak; recognizable fragments do not make these complete structures accessible. Score changes differ across seeds and do not consistently accompany a move toward more conventional chemistry.

applicability_conditions: The scored current graph must contain a removable acyclic substituent attached directly to a ring through a non-ring single bond. The Parent offers many such states, but some late cages do not; acyclic-only molecules and ring-to-ring connectors receive no added branch option.

The added removal is bounded by the actual connected substituent and inherited atom domain, with no newly calibrated branch-size setting. A long branch can be removed in one edit; no geometric or energetic accessibility claim follows from retaining its ring framework.

Whole-substituent deletion may remove an essential functional group or attachment geometry. Useful score retention requires accessible smaller alternatives, and observed Parent score ties across peripheral variants motivate rather than prove that condition.

Original single-leaf options remain available, and no new top-level operator weight, score preference or restart is added. The changed union redistributes only the already-selected deletion category's choices; accepted scores still determine later movement.

The current Parent does not contain the sulfur gate. The new sibling's confirmed chemical restriction and uneven score changes are evidence of a separate limitation, not permission to combine its mechanism into this Child.

All non-active Layer interfaces, task-local isolation, repaired identity handling and protocol-owned resources remain frozen. Generated alternatives are online edits of the actual current graph, never retrieved corpus molecules or additional evaluations.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecule by drawing atom, bond, path and ring edits, normalizing their molecular identities, and directly evaluating the first full batch allowed by inverse-motif memory. Both inverse signs from the same selected transition must match to veto a fresh neighbor. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph even when its score is worse, and a separate archive retains the best score. The current deletion choices remove one leaf atom or contract one degree-two atom, so removal of a longer pendant substituent requires several separately evaluated transitions. Identity normalization, memory lifetime and accepted-score selection are already established parts of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Extend the existing deletion menu with a whole pendant-branch choice. When the deletion operator is drawn, it may remove an entire acyclic substituent attached through one single bond to a ring atom, while retaining every ring atom and the connections among retained atoms. Single-leaf choices remain in the same menu, and the operator keeps its existing allocation weight. This adds direct compact neighbors that no existing one-step removal can reach. The earlier sulfur sibling filtered local valence; this experiment changes the size of a permitted deletion and does not inherit or add that filter.
